records.name: Creating Opportunities for All
records.summary: A career training nonprofit that teaches construction trades and computer skills such as engineering software. It has a youth track for ages 12 to 20 and a track for veterans.
records.what_you_do: Take a 24 week training program in construction or software skills, then join optional team projects. The youth track links to STEM and career technical classes.

cost.text: The site mentions free training and scholarships for the youth track. No prices are listed for the other tracks.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the website to ask about the next youth or veterans training start, or about scholarships
first_step.basis: Training is a set program, and the site does not explain how to enroll.

records.notes: IRS legal name is Creating Opportunities for Youth Empowerment Inc. The site brands itself Creating Opportunities for All (COFA), with a youth division (COFYE, ages 12 to 20) and a veterans division (COV). The site has no dated news or events, so status is probably_active by the working-site-with-no-dates rule. The only dates on the site are in staff bios and a 2026 footer, which are not evidence. The IRS list address (8030 Thouron Ave, 19150) does not appear on the site, so it is not published as a location. The site offers only a contact form and newsletter sign-up, with no email or phone.

records.name: Curricula for the Community
records.summary: A literacy nonprofit that tutors children ages 3 to 10 one on one and coaches families on reading at home. It also works with schools.
records.what_you_do: Families book one on one tutoring with a plan made for each child, or join family literacy sessions. Schools can book teacher training and small group sessions for students.

cost.text: The site does not say whether tutoring is free or paid, and lists no prices.

first_step.how: Book a consultation through the appointments page on the website, or send the contact form, and ask about one on one tutoring for a child ages 3 to 10
first_step.basis: Families start with a booked consultation, and the site lists no prices or class times.

records.notes: Legal name Curricula for the Community (IRS list). The site has no dated news or events, so status is probably_active by the working-site rule. Its public offers are mostly services for schools and families, and the site does not say whether they are free. The IRS list address (4953 N Hutchinson St, 19141) is not on the site, so it is not published as a location.

records.name: Fostering Success Boys to Men
records.summary: A nonprofit that coaches and mentors at-risk boys and young men through workshops, a youth leadership academy, and street outreach. It also runs transitional housing.
records.what_you_do: Young people and their caregivers can ask about the youth leadership academy, the rites of passage program, the STEM leaders program, and the workshops. The group also runs workshops for schools and other organizations.

cost.text: The site has a donation button. Program costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Send a message through the Chat with us form on the website, or call (267) 650-9616, and ask which youth program has a place open
first_step.basis: The site describes its programs but does not explain how a young person enrolls or who is eligible.

records.notes: The site says the group was established in 2016 and shows a 2024 copyright, neither of which is used as evidence of activity. The home page has no dated events or news, and the /events page returned 404. Transitional housing and group home services are listed, but the site does not explain eligibility. The IRS list address (5773 Kemble Ave, 19141) is not on the site, so it is not published as a location.

records.name: Friends 4 Life Foundation
records.notes: Held out, needs review. The IRS list address is 6106 N 7th St, 19120 (Philadelphia), but the site now gives a mailbox address in Elkins Park, Montgomery County. The home page names no Philadelphia program, and the Broadway on Broad Street event has no date or place. The 2026 Scholarship Winners heading gives only a year, so status active rests on the year alone. The /about page returned 404. If a Philadelphia program is confirmed, change the verdict to publish and write a summary. Legal name Friends 4 Life Foundation Inc.

records.name: Friends of the Oak Lane Library
records.notes: IRS list name is Friends of the Free Library of Philadelphia Inc, at 6614 N 12th St, which is the Oak Lane Library address. Search results (snippets only, not pages I could open) describe a separate 501(c)(3) called Friends of the Oak Lane Library that meets monthly and welcomes adults. The Free Library calendar page and the Oak Lane branch page both returned HTTP 403 to my fetch, so nothing from them is recorded. The IRS EIN is not confirmed as this group's. The search snippet also listed an email address that was not verified on a readable page. Verify on a readable page before publishing. No summary is written.

records.name: Hands Elevated for a Purpose
records.summary: Neighbors who provide personal care products to students in underserved parts of Philadelphia. They also share a list of free places for food and basic supplies and give children chances to explore beyond their neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the volunteer form on the website to help with the personal care and youth programs. Check the events page for job fairs and other dates.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the events page, such as a spring job fair on May 16, 2026. The site lists no weekly schedule.

cost.text: Donations go through PayPal. The site does not say what, if anything, recipients pay.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form linked on the website, or use the contact page to ask about the personal care products
first_step.basis: The volunteer form is open to anyone, but the site gives no details on what volunteering involves.

records.notes: The site brands itself H.E.L.P Inc. The IRS legal name is Hands Elevated for a Purpose. The event dates (August 3 2025, September 27 2025, January 17 2026, and the May 16 2026 spring job fair) come from event link addresses on the events page, not from visible text. The site says the group was founded in 2017. The Personal Care Project was marked to launch in spring 2025, so its current status is unclear. The IRS list address is an apartment, so it is not published.

records.name: Holy Family Formation and Education Center
records.summary: A faith formation center that runs religion classes for children from toddlers to teens, supports parents who raise their children in the faith, and trains catechists, the religion teachers.
records.what_you_do: Parents bring children to the formation programs, and new teachers can train as catechists. The site does not explain how to sign up.

first_step.how: Visit holyfamilycgs.org and ask how to enroll a child or train as a catechist. The site lists no phone number or email.
first_step.basis: The site gives no sign-up steps or contact details, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Newest dated item is a July 2025 post about new catechists, which is 15 months old. The 2026 footer is not used as evidence. The IRS list address (916 Plainfield St, 19150) is not shown on the site, so it is not published until a reviewer confirms it. The site lists its funder, a private foundation, but that is not a community group and is not recorded.

records.name: In the Eyes of Grieving Mothers

records.name: Jesus Christ in Power Ministries
records.summary: A congregation with Sunday school, Sunday worship, and weeknight services. It says everyone is welcome, including people who do not have a church home.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Sunday or weeknight service, join Sunday school, or send a prayer request through the form on the website. The site lists no volunteer program.

schedule.text: Sunday school at 10 am (April to September) or 11 am (October to March). Sunday service at 11 am (April to September) or 12 pm (October to March). Weeknight services on Wednesday at 7:30 pm, Thursday at 7 pm, and Friday at 6 pm. Communion is the first Sunday of each month.

cost.text: The site lists no fee. It accepts donations through a Cash App link.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday service, or call (267) 297-7179 to ask about times
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome, including people without a church home, and lists service times.

records.notes: The site shows Page updated with no date and no dated events, so status is probably_active. The Facebook and LinkedIn links in the footer belong to the web designer, so they are not recorded. The site shows no street address, so the IRS list address (1980 Church Ln, 19141) is not published until confirmed. The denomination is not stated, so faith is left blank.

notes: Searches: both used, on In the Eyes of Grieving Mothers and on the Oak Lane Friends group. The other IRS groups with no web address (Damirs, Entrepreneurs of America, Esthercares, Future Path, House of Wisdom-Chrida) got no search, so they are held as unknown with no summary. Generations Restored has a dead domain and is also held. Friends 4 Life is held as out_of_area for review because its current address is outside Philadelphia. Hands Elevated publishes its events-page dates, which come from link addresses. Every IRS address that is a home or apartment, or that the site does not show, is left out. The Free Library pages returned 403, so the Oak Lane Friends record stays held until verified. No rate limiting was seen on other domains. Records with status unknown and no summary are held back by design. Ran out of search budget before finishing the no-address IRS groups; this is the main gap.
